2.

Nanuet, New York 10954.  Plaintiff’s current residence address is 20510 Cypress

New Rochelle, New York.  Both vehicles were travelling southbound at the time of 
the occurrence.

6. 
That the serious and severe personal injuries sustained by plaintiff, JUSTIN SAPINI, 
were occasioned solely and wholly through and by reason of the carelessness, 
recklessness and negligence of the defendants in the ownership, operation, 
management, maintenance and control of the within motor vehicle; in operating same 
without due regard to the rights and safety of the plaintiff; in failing to properly steer, 
guide, manage and control said motor vehicle; in carelessly and negligently merging 
into plaintiff’s lane of travel without ensuring it was safe to do so; in carelessly and 
negligently operating the said motor vehicle over and along a public highway at a high 
and/or excessive rate of speed and/or at a greater rate of speed than care and caution 
would permit under the circumstances and conditions then and there existing to the 
knowledge of the defendants; in failing to maintain a safe and adequate distance from 
plaintiff’s vehicle; in failing to apply the brakes or slow down or stop in such a manner 
as would have prevented the occurrence; in failing to make adequate and timely 
observation of and response to conditions; in failing to keep a proper look-out when 
controlling said motor vehicle; in carelessly and negligently disregarding traffic 
control devices in place at the scene of the occurrence then and there in effect; in 
failing to see plaintiff’s vehicle; in driving into plaintiff’s vehicle; in driving into 
traffic without ensuring that it was safe to do so; in operating said motor vehicle in 
violation of the traffic rules, regulations, statutes and ordinances; in failing to avoid a 
collision with the plaintiff; and the defendant, ANTHONY F. FERRARA, was 
otherwise careless and negligent in failing and omitting to take proper and suitable 
precautions to avoid the said occurrence. Defendant, METRO-NORTH COMMUTER

Upon information and belief, the foregoing injuries including the symptoms, 
complaints, physical findings and disability herein alleged are permanent in nature. 
10. 
Plaintiff sought treatment at the emergency room at Montefiore Nyack Hospital, 
located at 160 N. Midland Avenue, Nyack, New York 10960 on April 24, 2023.   
11. 
As a result of the within accident, plaintiff, JUSTIN SAPINI, was confined as follows: 
(a) 
Bed: The plaintiff had been confined to his bed for approximately one (1) week 
following the within accident on April 23, 2023 and one (1) week following 
his left shoulder surgery, with the exception of necessary health care visits. 
 
(b) 
Home: The plaintiff has been essentially confined to his home from the date 
of accident of April 23, 2023, through present and continuing, with the 
exception of necessary health care visits. 
 
12. 
Plaintiff has been totally disabled and incapacitated from his employment from the 
date of accident of April 23, 2023 through present, and continuing. 
13. 
At the time of the within accident, plaintiff was working as a financial advisor for 
Northwestern Mutual, located at 875 Third Avenue, New York, New York 10022.  At 
the time of the accident, plaintiff was paid by commission only.  Plaintiff has not been 
able to return to work since the date of accident on April 23, 2023, through present.  
An exact loss of earnings will be provided upon retention of an economic expert.

1128(d), 1129(b), 1190, 1212, 1225(c)(d) and 1226 of the Vehicle and Traffic Laws

19. 
Upon information and belief, the foregoing injuries including the symptoms, 
complaints, physical findings and disability herein alleged are permanent in nature.  
Plaintiff sustained “serious injuries” as defined by Article 51 of the New York State 
Insurance Law in that plaintiff has suffered a permanent loss of use of a body organ, 
member, function or system; permanent consequential limitation of use of a body 
organ or member; significant limitation of use of a body function or system; or a 
medically determined injury or impairment of a non-permanent nature which prevents 
the injured person from performing substantially all of the material acts which 
constitute such persons usual and customarily daily activities for not less than ninety 
(90) days during the one hundred eighty (180) days immediately following the 
occurrence of the injury or impairment. 
20.
